critic.verdict: Film: a low-focused forward push down the lane keeps the boy silhouette coherent with no visible ghost, tearing or awkward layer clipping; the poster frame reads cleanly and the light-sweep is subtle and fitting for the lantern-lit dusk, keeping the hand-coloured engraving feel. It is meaningfully better than a plain centred push-in, expressing arrival into the street, though restrained. Plate: no stray text, no unwanted faces (boy is a rear silhouette as directed), no anachronisms, and no mangled anatomy or objects visible.

rounds.verdict: Do not publish as-is: technically clean, but the motion is too slight to express arrival in Chinatown beyond a plain push-in.
filmIssues: The move is coherent and the boy shows no tearing, ghosting or halo, but across all six frames it reads as a very timid plain push-in: zoom 1.0 to 1.1 produces almost no sense of travelling down the lane or of parallax separating the boy from the street.

The poster frame is a good opening picture and the warm light-sweep is fitting and subtle for lantern dusk, but the near-static progression would feel like a stall when scrubbed forwards and backwards.
No layer clips the frame edge awkwardly and the hand-coloured engraving style is preserved.

plan.rationale: A slow forward move down the lane, as if arriving with the family and coming to rest behind the small boy. Focusing low on him lets the nearer silhouette grow slightly more than the shophouse street through parallax, so he remains still and small while Singapore closes gently around him; a warm light-sweep echoes the dusk lanterns without inventing weather.
